Recurrent excitation, inhibition, and network regimes

Project 10. A modest random recurrent network of current-based leaky integrate-and-fire neurons, half the work of seeing a regime in a raster and half in the population signals (rate, synchrony, spectrum).

Model

||(N_E = 0.8 N||) excitatory cells and ||(N_I = 0.2 N||) inhibitory cells. Membrane and synapses: ||[ \tau_m \dot v = E_L - v + I_{\mathrm{syn}} + \sigma \sqrt{\tau_m}\,\xi ||]||[ \tau_{\mathrm{syn}} \dot I_{\mathrm{syn}} = -I_{\mathrm{syn}} ||]A spike resets ||(v||) to ||(V_{\mathrm{reset}}||) and starts a 2 ms refractory period. After a fixed axonal delay of 1 ms, an excitatory spike adds ||(+w_{\mathrm{exc}}||) to ||(I_{\mathrm{syn}}||) and an inhibitory spike adds ||(-w_{\mathrm{inh}}||). Each cell also receives 100 independent Poisson inputs at rate ||(\nu_{\mathrm{ext}}||) with weight 1 mV, so the sparsity slider changes recurrence without rescaling the external current. Fixed: ||(\tau_m = 20||) ms, ||(E_L = -70||) mV, ||(V_{\mathrm{th}} = -50||) mV, ||(V_{\mathrm{reset}} = -65||) mV. ||(\xi||) is unit white noise.

One network

Load a preset to set the six sliders, then change any of them. Run network simulates this connectivity and the same drive with ||(w_{\mathrm{exc}} = w_{\mathrm{inh}} = 0||). The label uses these fixed cuts, in order:
  • quiescent: rate ||(< 1||) Hz
  • runaway: rate ||(> 80||) Hz
  • inhibition-dominated suppression: rate ||(< 0.5||) times the uncoupled rate
  • oscillatory: spectral peak / median ||(\geq 8||) between 15 and 90 Hz
  • synchronized: synchrony ||(S \geq 2||) without that peak
  • otherwise asynchronous
||(S = \mathrm{std}(K) / \sqrt{\mathrm{mean}(K)}||) for population spike counts ||(K||) in 5 ms bins. Irregular independent spiking sits near ||(S \approx 1||). Presets are rough starting points from short runs at ||(N = 400||); a different ||(N||) or seed can cross a cut.

data.text/markdown:
Coupling phase diagram

Sweep a ||(6 \times 6||) grid of ||(w_{\mathrm{exc}}||) and ||(w_{\mathrm{inh}}||) at the drive, sparsity, ||(\tau_{\mathrm{syn}}||), noise, and seed currently set above. Each point uses ||(N = 200||) and 250 ms, then the same cuts as the single-network label. One extra run with both weights at zero supplies the uncoupled rate. This is a coarse sketch: short traces make the spectral cut noisy.

data.text/markdown: Click Run phase diagram to sweep coupling.

Takeaways

  • Recurrent excitation and inhibition do not just scale the firing rate. The same external drive can be quiet, asynchronous, synchronized, rhythmic, suppressed, or running away, depending on the two weights.
  • A raster shows who spiked. The population rate, ||(S||), and the spectrum say whether those spikes are shared, rhythmic, or only locally irregular.
  • The cuts are deliberate round numbers so the diagram stays readable. They are not a claim that real cortex falls into six sharp boxes.
